_comment: Extras for the worksheet /teachers/worksheets/grammar/wechselpraepositionen (French: places, à / en / au / chez, and the room words sur, sous, dans …), on top of the topic's own exercises: a position/movement rule (the keys keep their old names: regel.wo = position (être + place word), regel.wohin = movement (aller, mettre, ranger …), kasus = the label 'position' / 'movement'; regel.lage = two notes: no stand/lie in everyday French, and the same preposition for going and being), a mascot comic, and picture exercises on the room in src/components/arbeitsblatt/ZimmerSzene.astro (numbers 1–12 are the things in the picture). In segments, a string is text and {"a": [...]} is a gap with every accepted answer. French text carries a no-break space before ? ! : (written \u00a0).

wo.was: Place: it stays there. être plus a place word (sur, sous, dans, devant …).

wohin.was: Direction: you go there, or you put it there. French uses the same place words as for position.

lage.text: Everyday French doesn't say whether a thing stands, lies or hangs: est is enough. La bouteille et le livre sont sur la table. (Posé, accroché exist when you want to be precise.)

lage.form: same word for going and being
lage.text: Je suis à Paris. Je vais à Paris. Il est dans la cuisine. Il va dans la cuisine. Countries: en France, au Maroc, aux États-Unis. Fixed pairs: accrocher au mur, jeter à la poubelle.

regel.kurz: Position and movement take the same preposition: être à / aller à, être dans / mettre dans. Remember à + le = au and de + le = du: au-dessus du lit, à côté du bureau. Cities take à, feminine countries en, masculine countries au, plural countries aux; a person's home is chez: chez Aïcha.

tandemSoGehts: Cut the cards in the middle. Partner A takes the left half, Partner B the right half.
A builds question 1 from the tiles and reads it out: “Où va Lucie ?”

B only has tiles: the subject, the verb in its base form and the parts of the sentence. Build the answer and put the verb in the right form (va, est, sont, met). A choice tile looks like “à / en / au”: keep only the right one. Cities take à, feminine countries en, masculine countries au, plural countries aux; à + le becomes au.
Then B asks question 2 and A answers. Take turns. At the end, check with the answer sheet.
Now swap cards and do it all again, faster.

tandemKueche.title: Round 3: Tidy the kitchen
tandemKueche.hint: Bruno is tidying the kitchen. A has the picture with arrows and knows where everything goes. B only sees the mess. Don't show your picture!
tandemKueche.teil1: Part 1 (Where does he put it? Où est-ce qu'il le met ?): B asks, A answers. B writes the answer down.
tandemKueche.teil2: Part 2 (Where is it now? Où est-ce que c'est maintenant ?): Now A asks. B answers from their notes.

tandemBild.title: Round 2: Spot the differences
tandemBild.hint: A and B have almost the same room. Five things are in a different place. Take turns to describe your picture with _est_ or _sont_ and a *place word* (sur, sous, devant …). Tick every difference.
redemittel: Sur mon dessin, le chat _est_ *sous* la table.

zuZweit.title: In pairs: memory game
steps: A looks at the picture for 30 seconds. Then A covers the picture.
B asks: “Où est le portable ?” or “Où est l'horloge ?”
A answers: “Le portable est sous le lit.”
Five questions, then swap. Who gets more right?
